findings.independent_reason: For the irrational rotational mapping torus, the invariant unit-sphere area form descends and calibrates every nonzero pi2 map by its integer degree, so the systole is exactly 4pi while scalar curvature is 2. A compact round-product Riemannian covering would give a finite-index pure-translation deck subgroup. The Ricci splitting of the universal cylinder forces product isometries, which cannot remove the nontrivial irrational rotation in any nonzero deck power. This verifies every closedness/orientation/nonzero-pi2 hypothesis and contradicts precisely the printed compact-product statement. Its topology is excluded from the new gap theorem; Major central damage is not established. The universal-cylinder correction is consistent with the cited bounded primary-source record.

The original slab index range includes end slabs outside the permitted interior range. With m>A0/c0+2, T=4m and centers 4j for |j|<=m-1, the 2m-1 width-four slabs lie in the neck and their area lower bounds exceed A0. The separate C0 perturbation errors must be budgeted after comparing tensor norms; allocating epsilon^3/4 to each and epsilon/2 to each scalar-curvature loss gives the claimed final bounds. The neck remains unchanged and the limiting systolic conclusion follows. These are local indexing/tolerance errors, not a false uniform theorem or an unclosed main argument.

Minimization of a closed absolute H2 class with nonzero image in relative H2 forces an interior component because boundary-supported cycles have zero relative image; this supplies the intended argument without claiming a free-boundary minimizer is closed. The direct area count gives at most one essential spherical component when e^t A0<2A0 and hence chi<=2, including an empty set of finite splitting times. The pi2-zero systole convention and final nontriviality word are separate scope/wording clarifications. The report does not claim sharpness or a formal proof-assistant certification.
